Compile and synthesize are two questions in one request; the power question of a design is in the same request as its area and timing questions.
The five levels of area, power, and timing
The model chooses a level from the source code and the flow description, not an exact value.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  OVERVIEW

1 gate equivalent (GE) = the area of one NAND2 gate = 0.196608 µm² in NanGate 15 nm.
Power = dynamic + leakage power for the testbench stimulus.

Reachable frequency = 1 / (2 ns − worst slack), from the netlist synthesized at 500 MHz.
Example: 1.438 ns of slack gives 1 / 0.562 ns = 1.78 GHz.
One level of area or power is a factor of 10. No test design misses the 500 MHz target (slack level 1), reaches 4 GHz, or uses 10 mW or more.

The same 725 test questions, one per request. The three examples are development designs with their tool result.

Area levels are usable; power levels are not
Bars: exact level. Dashed line: the most common level of the tool labels.

Area: KEV-27B is exact for 61 of 92 designs and within one level for all 92; with examples the exact count drops to 48. Power: only KEV-4B without examples (39 of 85) is above always level 2 (37 of 85).
Timing levels: no model beats a constant answer
Bars: exact level. Dashed line: the most common tool level. No slack is negative.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  RESULTS
With examples KEV-27B reaches 36 of 92 (frequency) and 60 of 92 (slack); the constant answers score 45 and 63. KEV-0.8B’s 63 of 92 is level 5 for every design.
KEV-27B’s chosen levels do not match the tool’s levels
Designs at each level: the tool, then KEV-27B without and with examples. Equal counts are not correct answers.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  RESULTS

Without examples KEV-27B puts 90 of 92 designs in frequency level 1 and no design in power level 1 or 2. With examples the counts come closer to the tool’s, but the exact scores stay below the constant answer.
Pairs: KEV-27B with examples picks the better design
Two designs of one problem, A and B, asked in both orders. Always A scores 50%.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  RESULTS
With examples KEV-27B is right for 41 of 46 area, 35 of 44 power, and 11 of 12 frequency questions, and for 20 of 23 area pairs in both orders (17 without).
What the results support, and what to do next
Observations on dataset v1 and one fixed example set, not a guarantee for other designs or other examples.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  CONCLUSION

• Compile check: KEV-27B, 122 of 123, no examples needed.
• Failure reason: KEV-27B, 15 of 16, when the prompt says that synthesis failed.
• Area level: KEV-27B, 61 of 92 exact, all 92 within one level.
• Better of two designs: KEV-27B with examples, 41 of 46 (area), 35 of 44 (power).

• Synthesis check: at most 9 designs above always “yes”; KEV-27B misses 12 of 24 failures with examples, 20 without.
• Power, frequency, and slack levels: no score more than 2 designs above the constant answer.
• KEV-0.8B: one answer for every design in 6 of 10 questions with examples.

• Dataset v2: more synthesis failures of code that compiles, designs that miss the timing target, equal yes and no counts.
• Other example sets, and more than three examples.
• Jev 1.13 and other models under the same protocol.
• Thresholds and example sets chosen on the development split only.
KEV does not replace the tools: the best synthesis check misses 12 of 24 failures. KEV can screen compile errors and rank two designs.

Ranking score and probability error, yes/no checks
A model can rank well and still decide badly at the 0.5 threshold. Cells: no examples → three examples.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  APPENDIX
Chance = 0.5; perfect ordering = 1. The probability that a design that works gets a higher yes probability than a design that fails.
Mean squared error of the yes probability. Zero is perfect; a confident wrong answer costs more than an unsure one.
KEV-27B’s synthesis ranking score rises from 0.814 to 0.918 with examples, while its failure detection at 0.5 rises from 4 to 12 of 24.
Within one level, and mean level error
Within one level: higher is better. Mean level error: lower is better. Each cell: no examples → three examples.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  APPENDIX
Mean level error uses the probability-weighted expected level, not only the most likely level. The level ranges are decades, so one level is not a fixed physical error.
Pair questions: both orders, one order, neither
Counts per pair. Each pair has two answers, one per order. Each cell: no examples → three examples.
KEV v1.0  •  Dataset v1  •  runs of 15 and 16 October 2026  |  APPENDIX
The two correct letters of a pair are opposite, so “one order correct” means the same letter in both orders. A letter swap can still be wrong in both orders.
Design groups in the test split
The retained designs by the group of the dataset plan. Pairs come from the REvolution candidates.
